Ask a few questions about your product and your competitors, then write llmention.yaml with starter buyer questions you can edit. If you pass the answers as flags, init asks nothing.

Related commands:
  llmention run
  llmention quick

Output:
  Shows text you can read in your terminal.
  Use --json to get JSON for scripts and other programs.

Usage:
  llmention init [flags]

Examples:
llmention init
llmention init --brand Tabslip --category "AI API cost tracking" --competitors "Helicone (helicone.ai), Langfuse" --engines openai,anthropic
llmention init --dry-run --brand Acme

Flags:
      --brand string         Your product or company name
      --category string      What it helps with in a few words, used in the starter prompts
      --competitors string   Competitors, comma-separated; add a site in brackets: "Helicone (helicone.ai), Langfuse"
      --domain strings       Your website domains (optional)
      --engines strings      Providers to ask: openai, anthropic, google, perplexity, openrouter (all four through one key) or mock (default: the ones with a key in your environment)
      --force                Overwrite an existing llmention.yaml
  -h, --help                 help for init

Global Flags:
      --config string     Path to the config file
      --dry-run           Preview changes without performing them
      --include-meta      Wrap machine output as {data, meta} (commands that expose request metadata)
      --jq string         Transform stable JSON output with a jq expression (commands with machine output)
      --json              Output stable JSON instead of the human view
      --no-ansi           Disable all ANSI/control sequences in human output
      --no-color          Disable color in human output
      --no-pager          Never use a pager for long human output
      --no-prompt         Never block on an interactive prompt
      --plain             Print unstyled, copy-safe text (commands with human output)
      --quiet             Suppress non-essential output
      --template string   Render stable JSON output through a Go text/template (commands with machine output)
